title: UK tribunal forces government to confirm secret Apple encryption order
date_note: Published November 19; ruling described as made Thursday.
summary: According to TechCrunch, the UK Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's national-security argument against disclosure, so the government must confirm it issued a secret order requiring Apple to provide encrypted customer data. The Home Office has not confirmed the notice; Apple did not respond after the ruling. A final hearing on what can be released is expected next year.
plain: A UK tribunal ruled the government must admit it ordered Apple to give access to encrypted customer data.
exec: Shows government pressure on end-to-end encryption and the legal route for challenging it.
impact: First known time the government was compelled to confirm a secret technical order, per Liberty (TechCrunch).

validation.note: TechCrunch only; tribunal ruling itself not opened.

review.note: Tribunal ruling, Home Office unconfirmed, Apple no response, final hearing next year, Liberty first-known claim checked against TechCrunch
